name: Ring World: Saturn and its particle rings (J2000.0)
description: Saturn and five large moons (Titan, Rhea, Iapetus, Dione, Tethys) as point masses, initial states from JPL Horizons at J2000.0. The ring grains drawn around Saturn are a visual layer only: they are not simulated bodies.
frame: Ecliptic and mean equinox of J2000.0 (Horizons REF_PLANE=ECLIPTIC, REF_SYSTEM=ICRF); right-handed; the x-y plane is the ecliptic
origin: Barycentre of the included bodies (zero total momentum), shifted from the Solar System Barycenter
gSource: CODATA 2018 (JPL SSD Astrodynamic Parameters); the engine's fixed value

gm.source: JPL SSD Astrodynamic Parameters, DE440 (Park et al. 2021, AJ 161:105) (system GM) minus the listed moons' GM
gm.note: Saturn carries its own mass plus every moon not listed as a separate body, so the Saturn system GM equals the DE440 system GM used by the barycentre preset

radius.source: JPL SSD Planetary Physical Parameters, mean radius (Archinal et al. 2018)

state.note: Horizons geometric state relative to the Solar System Barycenter, km -> m by x1000, before the barycentre shift

omitted: the ring particles (drawn as massless visual grains, never integrated)
the Sun and every other planet
small Saturnian moons (their mass is lumped into Saturn)
Saturnian oblateness (J2), ring gravity and tides
assumptions: positions are DE441 vectors, masses are DE440 GM (the combined effect is measured by the committed validation tests)
m = GM / G, so the source GM is reproduced exactly

each planet with listed moons is represented by a center or system-barycentre state from Horizons; its mass is the DE440 system GM minus listed moon masses, so each listed system keeps its DE440 system GM
moon and planet states come from Horizons (CENTER=500@0), so they share one frame, epoch and origin and no planet-relative transformation is applied
the same Saturn-system states, GM and radii as the Solar System with major moons preset, re-centred on the barycentre of these six bodies
limitations: No Sun: the system is isolated, so Saturn does not orbit anything here
the rings are a visual layer; they exert no gravity and have no collisions
Newtonian point-mass orbits only: no oblateness, no resonance forcing beyond mutual gravity
